headline: Highest risk is dbt-core’s allowlisted egress touching warehouse data; prompt-injection and conflict risks are otherwise limited by the non-runnable awesome-selfhosted profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default instruction-bridging channel is documented. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while dbt-core’s documented surface is warehouse API access, not ingesting the other agent’s outputs as instructions.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies awesome-selfhosted content into dbt-core prompts or macros, injection risk appears.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or file sync.
Review any orchestrator that forwards text between agents.
Use explicit allowlists for dbt inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any bridged content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, so sensitive warehouse content can leave the local boundary through its API calls. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and touches no data, so it is not the leakage source; the pair risk is driven by dbt-core’s documented data flow.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes sensitive records, dbt-core can transmit them to the warehouse/API path.
IF an operator routes additional files into dbt-core, those contents may also be exposed.
mitigations: Restrict dbt projects to non-sensitive schemas.
Audit allowlisted egress destinations.
Run a dry-run on synthetic data first.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive warehouses.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound warehouse queries.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and exposes no filesystem or network write capability, while dbt-core only documents warehouse API calls and allowlisted egress, so a shared mutable-resource conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk would emerge.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, reassess for locking.
mitigations: Keep separate working directories.
Avoid shared git write access.
Use one-way data flow only.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can act on warehouse data, but awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge-management list and not runnable, so there is no documented chain where B blindly executes A’s outputs. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to convert list content into dbt inputs.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds awesome-selfhosted entries directly into dbt models without validation, cascade risk increases.
IF dbt artifacts are treated as authoritative without tests, downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Validate any imported list entries before use.
Require tests for dbt model changes.
Keep human review between the agents.
Use synthetic fixtures for integration checks.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core processes warehouse data and may therefore inherit retention or residency obligations, while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management artifact with no data handling. The pair risk is a compliance mismatch on the B side if warehouse data includes regulated classes; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated data classes, dbt-core must satisfy the corresponding residency/retention rules.
IF the deployment region or logging policy differs from the warehouse policy, compliance gaps appear.
mitigations: Confirm warehouse data classification.
Check retention settings on dbt logs and artifacts.
Document residency for all outbound queries.
Separate regulated and non-regulated projects.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for data-class-specific runs.
